correctness.rationale: Direct commutator multiplication is an invertible signed wedge map on rank-three free modules. For fixed nonzero target valuation s, the valuation-a images of u wedge (-) have cardinality q^{2(m-a)} and kernels q^{m+2a}; counting admissible u by its forced third coordinate yields the exact geometric series, valid over any finite chain ring. The zero-target formula follows from the same kernel ranks. Exhaustive cross-product fiber enumerations on ten small equal-/mixed-characteristic test cases agree with every target.

evidence: Stasinski, arXiv:1211.6872, Corollary 6.4: every trace-zero matrix over a principal ideal ring is a commutator (support, not fiber multiplicity).
Yuen, arXiv:math/0608632, Sections 2 and 5: jet schemes and dimension recursion of rank-one determinantal varieties, relevant to the zero cross-product fiber only.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Yuen controls the zero-target determinantal jets, and Stasinski establishes surjectivity for every target. Neither statement implies numerical nonzero fibers without further valuational enumeration. The new claim has stronger pointwise multiplicity information but not a stronger existence statement.

value.rationale: The all-target additive commutator measure refines the classical trace-zero surjectivity problem; it supplies exact probabilities at every valuation and shows a universal ring-independent profile across equal and mixed characteristic, not only zero-fiber counting or a trivial normalization. The arbitrary-depth and arbitrary-residue-field theorem supplies a natural complete distribution invariant.
